question: When was the Civil Service Act introduced in Nepal for the first time?
explanation: The Civil Service Act in Nepal was formally introduced for the first time on Bhadra 22, 2013 BS to bring a structured administrative framework to the government machinery[cite: 1].

question: In which year, M.N. Booch commission on administration reform was constituted in Nepal?
explanation: The M.N. Booch Administrative Reform Commission was constituted in the year 2000 BS to recommend improvements and modernization in public administration[cite: 1].

question: Civil service Act in Nepal was introduced under the leadership of prime minister of:
explanation: The landmark Civil Service Act was enacted and introduced under the premiership and leadership of Tanka Prasad Acharya[cite: 1].

question: Under whose leadership was the High level Administrative Reform Commission, 2048 constituted?
explanation: The High-Level Administrative Reform Commission of 2048 BS was formed under the leadership of then Prime Minister Girija Prasad Koirala[cite: 1].

question: The Government of Nepal has started celebrating civil service day since:
explanation: Nepal officially started celebrating National Civil Service Day annually beginning in the year 2061 BS[cite: 1].

question: From which amendment of civil service act has the provision to make civil service inclusion begun?

options.a: The provision was there from beginning

explanation: Inclusion and reservation policies within the Nepalese civil service were formally introduced and initiated through the second amendment of the Civil Service Act[cite: 1].

question: Public service commission was established in competition for the first time?
explanation: The Public Service Commission (Loksewa Aayog) was established and began conducting competitive examinations in 2008 BS[cite: 1].

question: Which country started the concept of civil service?
explanation: China is historically recognized as the pioneer country that originated the foundational concepts of a formal civil service examination and merit-based bureaucracy[cite: 1].

question: Since, when the Civil Service Act, 2049 came into effect?
explanation: The Civil Service Act, 2049 officially came into enforcement and effect on 2050/02/04 BS[cite: 1].

question: How many chapters and sections are there in the civil service Act - 2049?
explanation: The Civil Service Act, 2049 is structured across 10 chapters containing a total of 76 sections[cite: 1].

question: How many times has the Civil Service Act -2049, been amended so far?
explanation: The Civil Service Act, 2049 has undergone a total of 4 amendments to date to accommodate administrative reforms[cite: 1].

question: In which part of the Constitution of Nepal is Public service commission incorporated?
explanation: The constitutional provisions relating to the Public Service Commission are enshrined under Part 23 of the Constitution of Nepal[cite: 1].

question: In which article of the constitution of Nepal, the formation of the Government Civil Service system is included?
explanation: Article 285 of the Constitution of Nepal outlines the provisions for the formation and operation of the Government Civil Service[cite: 1].

question: Reservation for the scheduled castes and scheduled tribes in the public services has been provided in the present Constitution of Nepal under
explanation: Article 285 of the Constitution incorporates provisions ensuring inclusive representation and reservation in government services[cite: 1].

question: According to the Civil Service Act, 2049, "Permanent post" means, a post of the civil service which is;

options.b: of which term is not specified

explanation: Under the Civil Service Act, 2049, a permanent post is defined as a pensionable position where the term of employment is not explicitly specified[cite: 1].

question: How many types of civil service have provisioned in Civil Service Act-2049?
explanation: The Civil Service Act, 2049 provisions a total of 10 distinct types of civil services (such as administrative, engineering, agricultural, etc.)[cite: 1].

question: According to the Civil Service Act, 2049 and the Civil Service Rules, 2050, how many groups are there under the Nepal Administrative Service?
explanation: The Nepal Administrative Service comprises 3 functional groups under the prevailing civil service rules[cite: 1].

question: How many groups are formed under the Nepal Engineering Service as per the Civil Service Rules, 2050?
explanation: The Nepal Engineering Service is organized into 15 specialized groups under the Civil Service Rules, 2050[cite: 1].

question: Under which ministry does the operational jurisdiction of the General Sub-group of the Engineering Group in the Nepal Engineering Service fall?

options.a: Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration
options.b: Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport
options.c: Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation

explanation: The operational mandate and jurisdiction of the General Sub-group within the Nepal Engineering Service fall under the Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport[cite: 1].

question: How many Classes of Gazette Officer have been provisioned by the Civil service Act in Nepal?
explanation: The Civil Service Act recognizes 3 main regular classes for Gazetted Officers (Gazetted Third Class, Second Class, and First Class, excluding Special Class)[cite: 1].

question: How many times has the civil service rules been amended so far?
explanation: The Civil Service Rules, 2050 have been amended 15 times to keep pace with administrative updates[cite: 1].

question: How many classes are there in non-gazette level of civil service of Nepal?
explanation: There are 5 classes in the non-gazette level of the Nepalese civil service ranging from Non-Gazetted Fourth Class up to First Class (and helpers/sardar levels as structured)[cite: 1].

question: Which section of the Civil service Act, 2049 has provisioned about fulfillment of Vacancy in service under the three chapters?
explanation: Section 7 of the Civil Service Act, 2049 contains provisions regarding the fulfillment of vacancies in the civil service[cite: 1].

question: According to civil service Act-2049, what percent of allocation has been made for gazette third class in the free competition?
explanation: For Gazetted Third Class positions, 70% of vacant posts are allocated for open/free competition[cite: 1].

question: According to civil service Act-2049, what percent of allocation has been made for non-gazette first class in the open competition?
explanation: Open competition allocation for non-gazette first class posts is set at 40% under the Act[cite: 1].

question: What percent of the total vacant post are recruited by open competition in the non-gazette first level of civil service of Nepal?
explanation: Recruitment via open competition for the specified non-gazette first level accounts for 40% of vacancies[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Act- 2049, what percent of allocation has been made for non-gazette second class in the free competition?
explanation: For non-gazette second class positions, 70% of vacancies are filled through free/open competition[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Act- 2049, what percentage of reservation should be made during recruitment of staff in Civil service in Nepal in the free competition?
explanation: A total reservation pool of 45% is allocated for inclusive groups during recruitment through open competition[cite: 1].

question: According to civil service Act - 2049, what percent of allocation has been made for gazette first class in the free competition?
explanation: For Gazetted First Class posts, open free competition accounts for 10% of the vacant positions[cite: 1].

question:
Match the following as per the provision of Civil Service Act, 2049 (reservation incorporated in the second amendment).
Group A: a. Backward region, b. Disabled, c. Dalits, d. Madhesi | Group B: 1. 9.0%, 2. 4.0%, 3. 22.0%, 4. 5.0%
explanation: Under the 45% reservation breakdown: Backward region is 4.0% (a2), Disabled is 5.0% (b4), Dalits are 9.0% (c1), and Madhesi are 22.0% (d3), making combination (d) correct[cite: 1].

question: How many districts has the Civil Service Act-2049, covered under backward area?
explanation: The Civil Service Act defines 9 remote districts as backward areas for regional reservation benefits[cite: 1].

question: Which district doesn't belong to Backward Area?
explanation: Rukum is not classified under the 9 designated backward districts (whereas Accham, Kalikot, and Jumla are part of them)[cite: 1].

question: Which section of the Civil service Act-2049, has provisioned about disqualifications for holding candidate under chapter three?
explanation: Section 10 of the Civil Service Act, 2049 specifies the disqualifications required for candidates applying to civil service posts[cite: 1].

question: The minimum age required for entering into gazette post of government of Nepal is;
explanation: The minimum age limit for entering Gazetted positions in the Government of Nepal is 21 years[cite: 1].

question: As per the provisions of Civil Service Rules 2050, within how many days from the date of recommendation for appointment to a vacant post of the Non Gazette through open or internal competition, the appointing authority must issue the appointment letter?
explanation: The appointing authority must issue the appointment letter within 15 days of recommendation for non-gazette posts[cite: 1].

question: For how long is the probation period for a new permanent employee in Civil Service?

options.b: 1 year for men and 6 months for women

explanation: The probation period for newly appointed permanent civil servants is 1 year for male employees and 6 months for female employees[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Act-2049, the tenure of the Chief Secretary of Nepal is
explanation: The maximum tenure for the Chief Secretary of Nepal is fixed at 3 years under the Civil Service Act[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Act -2049, what is the age limitation for the retirement of a civil servant in Nepal?
explanation: The standard compulsory retirement age limit for civil servants under the Act is 58 years[cite: 1].

question: As per the provisions of Civil Service Act 2049, in how much percentage of posts is there a provision for promotion through performance evaluation?
explanation: A 40% allocation of promotional posts is designated for promotion based on performance evaluation[cite: 1].

question: What is the maximum number of marks that can be obtained for seniority for promotion of employees working in Civil Service?
explanation: A maximum of 30 marks is allocated for work seniority during the civil service promotion evaluation[cite: 1].

question: According to the Civil Service Rules 2050, how many marks are provided for service in geographical region while promoting an employee?
explanation: A maximum of 16 marks is awarded for service experience in designated geographical remote regions during promotion[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Act 2049, maximum evaluation mark that may be granted by the supervisor.
explanation: The supervisor can grant a maximum of 25 evaluation marks for performance appraisal[cite: 1].

question: The registration of the trade union of civil employees shall be made in the

options.b: Department of labour and employment promotion
options.c: Ministry of federal affairs and general administration

explanation: Trade unions representing civil employees are required to register with the Department of Labour and Employment Promotion[cite: 1].

question:
Which of following given statement is/are correct?
I. First amendment in Civil Service Act- 2049, provided trade Union rights to civil servants ranking gazette third class level and below.
II. In 2064 B.S., Second amendment in Civil Service Act- 2049, provisioned for the reservation of women and marginalized ethnic groups and communities.
explanation: Both statements are correct: the first amendment granted trade union rights up to gazetted third class, and the second amendment in 2064 BS introduced reservations for women and marginalized groups[cite: 1].

question: Which section of the Civil Service Act, 2049 has provisioned 'relating to professional organization of civil employees' under the Chapter Seven?
explanation: Section 53 of the Act contains provisions relating to professional organizations and trade unions of civil employees[cite: 1].

question: From which amendment of Civil service Act-2049, civil servants are prohibited from acquiring foreign permanent residency through diversity visa?
explanation: The 4th amendment introduced strict restrictions prohibiting civil servants from acquiring permanent residency abroad or DV/PR[cite: 1].

question: Which chapter of the Civil Service Act -2049, has provisioned about the code of conduct?
explanation: Chapter 7 of the Civil Service Act, 2049 outlines the professional code of conduct for civil employees[cite: 1].

question: Which section of the Civil Service Act, 2049 has provisioned about the 'Statement of property' under the Chapter 7?
explanation: Section 54 mandates the regular submission of property and asset statements by civil servants[cite: 1].

question: Which section of the civil service Act,-2049, has provisioned about the restriction on critic government under the chapter seven?
explanation: Section 45 restricts civil employees from making public criticisms or statements against government policies and actions[cite: 1].

question: "No civil employee shall subject any one to torture", which section of chapter seven deals with this statement?
explanation: Section 54 A explicitly prohibits any civil employee from subjecting anyone to physical or mental torture[cite: 1].

question: Which of the following punishment is not included in the ordinary punishments that may subjected to the departmental punishments to the employees of Civil Service?

options.b: Withholding of promotion for two years or withholding of two salary increments
options.c: Withholding of two to five salary increments
options.d: Removal from service, without being disqualified for government service in the future.

explanation: Removal from service is classified as a major/special departmental punishment rather than an ordinary minor punishment[cite: 1].

question: In which of the following circumstances, a civil employee may be removed from service without being disqualified for government service in the future if he/she?

options.c: frequently violates the matters relating to conduct

explanation: Committing frequent acts of indiscipline, participating in politics, or repeatedly violating the code of conduct are grounds for removal from service without future disqualification[cite: 1].

question: Which of following punishment is subjected to a civil employee, if his/her performance didn't found satisfactory?

options.b: withholding of promotion for upto two years
options.c: withholding of a maximum of two salary increments

explanation: Unsatisfactory performance can lead to departmental penalties including censure, withholding of promotion, or withholding salary increments[cite: 1].

question: In which of the following circumstances, a civil employee may be dismissed from service, with being disqualified for government service in the future, if he/she?

options.a: convicted by a court of a criminal offence involving moral turpitude
options.b: obtain or apply for a permanent residence permit

explanation: Criminal convictions involving moral turpitude, obtaining foreign PR, or committing corruption are grave offenses leading to dismissal with future disqualification[cite: 1].

question: According to the Civil Service Act 2049, leave is merely; a/an:
explanation: Under the civil service framework, taking leave is treated strictly as a privilege rather than an absolute enforceable right[cite: 1].

question: How many types of leave are provided under the Civil Service Act, 2049?
explanation: The Civil Service Act, 2049 provides for 9 distinct types of leave for civil employees[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Rules 2050, there is a provision that employees can get festival leave without increasing it by days throughout the year..
explanation: Festival leave is provisioned for 6 days per year without accumulation or carryover[cite: 1].

question: What does a suspended employee get during the period of suspension from the regular job, as per to Civil Service Act, 2049?

options.a: Half of the salary amount and festival allowance
options.b: Half of the salary amount and half of the festival allowance
options.c: One fourth of the salary amount and festival allowance

explanation: During the period of suspension, an employee is entitled to receive half of their regular salary amount subsistence allowance[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Rules-2050, how many days civil servant can get sick leave per year?
explanation: Civil servants are entitled to 12 days of sick leave annually under the Civil Service Rules[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Rules 2050, In cases where a female civil employee becomes pregnant how many days of maternity leave is there before or after the birth that such an employee is allowed to take?
explanation: Female civil employees are granted 98 days of paid maternity leave around childbirth[cite: 1].

question: According to the civil service rules, if the wife of a male civil servant gives birth, how many days of maternity care leave can such an employee be allowed to take before or after the delivery?
explanation: Male civil servants are entitled to 15 days of paternity/maternity care leave around the time of childbirth[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Rules 2050, how many days can an employee accumulate the vacation leave he/she has earned?
explanation: Earned home/vacation leave can be accumulated up to a maximum limit of 180 days[cite: 1].

question: According to Civil Service Act-2049, which of the following leave can get by Civil servants?
explanation: Civil servants are eligible for all the listed leave categories including festival, home, and study leave[cite: 1].

question: How many years of permanent service period should an employee has completed to get study leave?
explanation: An employee must complete at least 3 years of continuous permanent service to qualify for study leave[cite: 1].

question: Which of the following leave is not available to an employee of the Civil Service?
explanation: Visit leave is not recognized as a standard leave category under the Civil Service Act and Rules[cite: 1].

question: Who approves the extraordinary leave of a civil servant?
explanation: Extraordinary leave for civil servants requires formal approval from the Government of Nepal (Cabinet level)[cite: 1].

question: Which ministry acts as the central body for the management and operation of civil service and employees?

options.c: Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration

explanation: The Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration (MoFAGA) serves as the central central agency for civil service management[cite: 1].

question: Who will approve study leave in Civil Service?
explanation: The approval authority for study leave in the civil service rests with the Government of Nepal[cite: 1].
